name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,556

clue.text: Sack cleaner holding up key centre of worship

indicators.note: to sack a place is to ransack and wreck it, so the following word is thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the Tab key on a keyboard
the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A sacked church cleaner is propping something up in a place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the reshuffled cleaner sits below the key, so it is holding it up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabernacle is a tent or building used as a sanctuary, a meeting house for religious services.

clue.text: Medication husband nicked from quay inside of marina

indicators.note: something nicked is stolen, so a letter is taken away from the word that follows
the inside of a word is its interior, everything except the first and last letters

blocks.note: a wharf is a quay
H is the standard abbreviation for husband
the word with its first and last letters dropped

explanation.surface: A husband pinches some medicine from a quay at the marina.
explanation.definitionFit: Warfarin is an anticoagulant drug prescribed to thin the blood and prevent clots.

clue.text: Quite cunning to seal off vent

indicators.note: sealing something off means enclosing it, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: fly is British slang for sharp or cunning
to vent an opinion is to air it

explanation.surface: A wily person contrives to block off a ventilation outlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Both work as adverbs of moderate degree: fairly good and quite good say the same thing.

clue.text: Complaint when tyres burst right away

indicators.note: a burst tyre is ruptured, so its letters come out in a jumbled order
something sent away is gone, so that letter is removed from the fodder

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles when their car tyres blow out and the right one goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a small inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a minor medical ailment or disorder.

clue.text: Mum in bother with desire for playwright

indicators.note: one word goes in, inside the other one

blocks.note: drat is a mild exclamation of annoyance, like bother
ma is an informal word for mother
an urge is a strong desire

explanation.surface: A mother in a fix has a yearning to become a dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum goes inside bother after its third letter, then desire follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramaturge is a writer or adapter of plays, especially one attached to a theatre company.

clue.text: Official regret about old soldiers appearing in court

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the preceding word is read backwards
the soldiers turn up inside the abbreviation for court

blocks.note: to rue something is to regret it
O is a standard abbreviation for old
CT is the abbreviation for court
the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment

explanation.surface: A functionary is sorry that some veterans have turned up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: Old gives just O; the soldiers then sit inside CT, the abbreviation for court.
explanation.definitionFit: A eurocrat is a bureaucrat or administrator working for the European Union's institutions.

clue.text: Food plate slyly hidden regularly by Australian

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the phrase is kept

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters
A is the abbreviation for Australian

explanation.surface: An Australian sneakily conceals a plate of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is a Spanish rice dish cooked with saffron, seafood or chicken in a wide pan.

clue.text: Digitally experienced material

blocks.note: first meaning: sensed by touch with the fingers, the digits
second meaning: a matted woollen fabric

explanation.walkthrough: Digitally suggests computers, but here it means with the fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of a verb of touching, and a noun for pressed, matted wool cloth.

clue.text: One who reprimands Mark goes very pale

indicators.note: the letter for mark departs, so it is removed from the word before it

blocks.note: one as the indefinite article
someone who lambasts, criticising harshly
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A person giving someone a dressing-down turns white as the target walks off.
explanation.walkthrough: One gives just A, then the reprimander loses his M.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a smooth white stone, so used as an adjective it describes a whitish complexion.

clue.text: Packing sausages is common practice

indicators.note: the word packs, or holds inside it, the letters needed

blocks.note: letters two to six of this word

explanation.surface: Stuffing sausages is a routine job.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage means habitual or customary procedure, the way something is normally done.

clue.text: Impose recycling of essentially bin-end stuff

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the central letters are kept
recycling sends something back round, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: the two central letters of the six
to stuff something into a bag is to force it in

explanation.surface: Insist that people recycle the dregs left over from wine sales.
explanation.walkthrough: A bin-end is a leftover bottle of wine sold off cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: To enforce a law or rule is to compel people to obey it, imposing it on them.

clue.text: Cat returns to eat lion, maybe seen via satellite

indicators.note: a word that returns goes back the way it came, so it is read right to left
maybe signals a possible variant of the word, so its letters are rearranged
eating takes something inside, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat
the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A house cat comes back to devour a lion, perhaps as filmed from space.
explanation.walkthrough: The satellite is not a spacecraft but the Moon, our natural satellite.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moonlit is illuminated by light from the Moon, the Earth's only natural satellite.

clue.text: Irritable and sarcastic when starting direction switched

indicators.note: the compass point at the front is swapped for a different compass point

blocks.note: sarky is British slang for sarcastic; its first letter S is south
north replaces south

explanation.surface: Someone tetchy and mocking when they change course at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: Narky is informal British slang for bad-tempered, cross or easily annoyed.

clue.text: Consequences of pursuing US subject

blocks.note: to be after someone is to pursue them
Americans say math where Britons say maths

explanation.surface: What follows from studying a subject at an American college.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftermath is the period of results and effects that follows a significant, usually unpleasant, event.

clue.text: London building a large place to sleep everyone

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a berth is a bunk on a ship or train
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A big London venue with room for everybody to bed down.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Albert Hall is a famous concert venue in Kensington, London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Albert Hall is a large domed concert hall in Kensington, home of the Proms.

clue.text: Pig's ear topping ex-PM's potato bites

blocks.note: making a pig's ear of something is British slang for making a hash of it, a mess
Gordon Brown, former British prime minister, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: An offal snack sits on a former prime minister's plate of potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, so it is topping it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hash browns are fried patties of grated or chopped potato, a breakfast staple.

clue.text: Stories are racy, but lent out by school head

indicators.note: letters let out are set loose and scattered into another order
the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written
its first letter

explanation.surface: A headteacher has lent out some risque tales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canterbury Tales is Chaucer's collection of narratives told by pilgrims travelling to Canterbury.

clue.text: Classic novel and French articles upset Macron?

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: Jane Austen's novel
le and un, French for 'the' and 'a'

explanation.surface: An old book and some French newspaper pieces annoy the French president.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: the French president's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmanuel is the first name of the French president Macron, so he exemplifies it.

clue.text: Revolutionary squats in inelegant retro housing

indicators.note: the phrase houses, or holds within it, a run of consecutive letters
retro means looking backwards, so the run is read in reverse

blocks.note: a run of letters across the three words

explanation.surface: A radical squats somewhere in clumsy, old-fashioned accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Leninist follows the doctrine of Lenin, leader of Russia's Bolshevik revolution of 1917.

clue.text: PC way to trade green car adopted by setter

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so the car goes inside the setter

blocks.note: eco- means environmentally friendly
the setter refers to themself as me
short for a Mercedes

explanation.surface: A politically correct business adopts an environmentally friendly vehicle from the compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like political correctness but means personal computer.
explanation.definitionFit: E-commerce is buying and selling goods online, a method of doing business by computer.

clue.text: Forecaster caught abandoning boat

indicators.note: the letter abandons the word, leaving it behind, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: a coracle is a small round wicker boat
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A weatherman is captured while jumping ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is a prophet or seer who foretells the future, as at ancient Delphi.

clue.text: Good (but not the best) category for somewhere to stay

definitions.text: Good (but not the best) category for somewhere to stay

blocks.note: surface reading: a decent second-tier grading for a hotel
setter's reading: the letter for a second-best grade, given twice and joined

explanation.surface: A guide awards lodgings a respectable but not top rating.
explanation.walkthrough: A grade B is good but not the best A; two of them, linked by 'and', name modest lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed and breakfast is a guesthouse offering a room overnight plus a morning meal.

clue.text: Stream clip here to see Boris?

indicators.note: clipping trims both ends, so only the inner letters survive

blocks.note: a beck is a northern English word for a brook
its first and last letters trimmed off

explanation.surface: Go to a brook to catch sight of a man called Boris.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris is not Johnson but the German tennis champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Becker is the German tennis player who won Wimbledon at seventeen, so a Boris exemplifies it.

clue.text: Firm can shut when ruined

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so these letters are broken up and reordered

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A company can close down when it goes bust.
explanation.definitionFit: Staunch means steadfast and loyal, as in a firm or unwavering supporter.

clue.text: Season Six avoids tax, originally set around Luxembourg

indicators.note: originally points to the origin, the very first letter
the numeral steers clear of the tax, so its letters are taken out
what remains of the tax wraps around the abbreviation

blocks.note: its first letter
value added tax
six in Roman numerals
L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg

explanation.surface: Six people dodge taxes, setting up their base in Luxembourg for the season.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT, value added tax, loses V and I, and the remaining two letters go around L.
explanation.definitionFit: To season food is to flavour it, and salt is the commonest flavouring, so it works as a verb.

clue.text: New supermarket across Norway impossible, I'm afraid

indicators.note: the shop spreads across the abbreviation, covering it on both sides

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
Ocado is a British online grocery retailer
N is the vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: A new store opening up across Norway won't happen, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is an informal reply refusing a request: it cannot be done, sorry.

clue.text: Gas planets get hot internally close to sun

indicators.note: internally points at the very centre of each word, its middle letter
the close of a word is its end, so its last letter is taken

blocks.note: the fourth of its seven letters
the central letter
the central letter
its final letter

explanation.surface: Gaseous planets heat up inside as they near the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is a noble gas, an inert chemical element used in glowing advertising signs.

clue.text: Flanders city romance featuring two lecturers

indicators.note: a story featuring characters holds them inside it

blocks.note: to romance is to tell fanciful untruths
L is the abbreviation for lecturer, here doubled

explanation.surface: An affair between two academics in a Flemish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Lille is a city in French Flanders, the historic region straddling France and Belgium.

clue.text: They watch attractive people running

blocks.note: a looker is an informal word for a good-looking person
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: Spectators gaze at beautiful joggers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lookers-on are spectators or bystanders observing an event without taking part.
